Psychrometric constant

Source: R/forcing-derived.R
ef_psychrometric.Rd

Computes the psychrometric constant \(\gamma\) of FAO-56 from the atmospheric pressure, with the latent heat of vaporization fixed at 2.45 MJ kg-1 as in the standardized reference evapotranspiration equation.

Usage

ef_psychrometric(pressure)

Arguments

pressure

Numeric. Atmospheric pressure \(P\) [kPa], for example from ef_air_pressure(). Must be finite and > 0.

Value

A numeric vector of the psychrometric constant \(\gamma\) [kPa degC-1] with the length of pressure, keeping its dim.

Details

$$\gamma = \frac{c_p P}{\varepsilon \lambda} = 0.665 \times 10^{-3} P$$ with \(c_p\) = 1.013e-3 MJ kg-1 degC-1, \(\varepsilon\) = 0.622 and \(\lambda\) = 2.45 MJ kg-1 (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 8). The coefficient published by FAO-56, 0.665e-3, is the rounded value of 1.013e-3 / (0.622 * 2.45) = 6.6475e-4 and is used as published (it is the one used in the FAO-56 examples).

Assumption: constant latent heat of vaporization (2.45 MJ kg-1, about 20 degrees C), as in the standardized equation. The general form with a temperature-dependent \(\lambda\) (FAO-56 annex 3, Eq. 3-10) is not implemented here.

Missing values propagate. Non-numeric or empty input raises earthflux_input_error; non-positive or infinite pressures raise earthflux_domain_error.

Verification status

VERIFICADA (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 8; dev/specs/weather-forcing.md 4.2, case V1: P = 81.8 kPa gives 0.054 kPa degC-1). The same coefficient, \(\gamma = 0.000665 P\), is ASCE-EWRI (2005) Eqs. 4 and 35 (pp. 10, 28), with \(\lambda\) = 2.45 MJ kg-1 (pp. 9, 27); the pressure of ef_air_pressure() is its Eqs. 3 and 34.

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

ASCE-EWRI (2005). The ASCE Standardized Reference Evapotranspiration Equation. Task Committee on Standardization of Reference Evapotranspiration, Environmental and Water Resources Institute of the American Society of Civil Engineers. Final report, January 2005. Published as Allen, R. G., Walter, I. A., Elliott, R. L., Howell, T. A., Itenfisu, D., Jensen, M. E., & Snyder, R. L. (Eds.), American Society of Civil Engineers, Reston, VA. doi:10.1061/9780784408056

See also

Other derived meteorological variables: ef_dewpoint(), ef_ea, ef_es(), ef_es_slope(), ef_ra_daily(), ef_ra_period(), ef_rso(), ef_wind_2m()

Examples

# FAO-56 example 2: elevation 1800 m
ef_psychrometric(ef_air_pressure(1800))
#> [1] 0.0543676
